metricHelp.activeRoutes: Count of route plans with status IN_PROGRESS — routes currently being executed by drivers.
metricHelp.totalRoutes: Total route plans in the system: PLANNED + IN_PROGRESS + COMPLETED.
metricHelp.deliveryProgress: Delivered stops ÷ total stops across all active routes × 100. A stop counts as delivered when its order status is DELIVERED.
metricHelp.ordersOnRoute: Orders with status ON_ROUTE — assigned to a route, departed, and not yet delivered.
metricHelp.totalOrders: Sum of orders across all pipeline stages (Received through Delivered).
metricHelp.activeDistance: Σ totalDistanceKm for IN_PROGRESS routes. Distance comes from optimized nearest-neighbor TSP legs (warehouse → stops → warehouse).
metricHelp.activeDuration: Σ totalDurationMin for IN_PROGRESS routes. Includes drive time (OSRM/Google + Jakarta traffic model) plus per-stop service time.
metricHelp.activeEmissions: Σ estimatedEmissionsKg for IN_PROGRESS routes. CO₂e ≈ distance × engine factor (EV 0.05, gasoline 0.15, diesel 0.22 kg/km).
metricHelp.avgDti: Mean Delivery Trip Index across delivered orders with complete timestamps. DTI = 100 − min(100, max(0, slackMin) × {penalty}) where slack = actualLead − plannedLead (receivedAt → deliveredAt vs planned ETA).
metricHelp.avgCfi: Mean Carbon Footprint Index across active and completed routes. CFI = 100 × (dieselKg − actualKg) ÷ (dieselKg − evKg) on the same distance. 100 = EV-equivalent, 0 = diesel.
metricHelp.activeDrivers: Number of drivers in the roster (each linked to one fleet vehicle).
metricHelp.tripFuelCost: Σ trip fuel cost for IN_PROGRESS routes. ICE: (distance ÷ km/L) × Pertamina price; EV: distance × kWh/km × PLN rate. Product matched by vehicle type + engine.
metricHelp.fuelSavings: Σ fuel savings vs naive baseline for IN_PROGRESS routes. Baseline = separate warehouse round-trip per stop (2 × distance × 1.35). Savings = baseline cost − optimized route cost.
metricHelp.pipelineReceived: Orders with status RECEIVED — accepted, awaiting warehouse prep.
metricHelp.pipelinePreparing: Orders with status PREPARING — being packed at the warehouse.
metricHelp.pipelineOnRoute: Orders with status ON_ROUTE — assigned to a route and en route to the recipient.
metricHelp.pipelineDelivered: Orders with status DELIVERED — confirmed handover to recipient.
metricHelp.totalVehicles: Total vehicles registered in the fleet database.
metricHelp.avgVqi: Mean Vehicle Quality Index. VQI = 100 − (age + odometer + cost + planning penalties). Higher is healthier; max penalty per factor is capped at 30/30/20/20 pts.
metricHelp.highRisk: Vehicles with VQI below {threshold} — prioritize maintenance or replacement.
metricHelp.mediumRisk: Vehicles with VQI {highBelow}–{lowAbove} — schedule inspection soon.
metricHelp.lowRisk: Vehicles with VQI above {threshold} — within acceptable health range.
metricHelp.upcomingMaintenance: Sum of estimated next-service costs for vehicles with predicted maintenance within the next 90 days.
metricHelp.fleetMaintenanceBudget: Sum of maintenanceCostUnit across all vehicles — total recorded maintenance spend per fleet unit.

methodology.title: Routing metrics & guide
methodology.subtitle: How Jakarta last-mile route optimization works — from order assignment and CSV import to traffic-aware ETAs, DTI/CFI delivery metrics, Pertamina fuel costing, and VQI-based driver dispatch.

distance.title: Reduce travel distance
distance.body: Nearest-neighbor TSP orders stops from the Blok M warehouse so couriers do not repeatedly cross Jakarta.

eta.title: Realistic ETAs
eta.body: Time estimates use OSRM with Jakarta rush-hour calibration (06:30–10:00 & 16:00–20:00 WIB), or Google live traffic when available.

vehicle.title: The right vehicle
vehicle.body: CAR_ONLY stops go to cars and MOTORCYCLE_ONLY stops to motorcycles; BOTH stops are divided to keep routes feasible.

fleet.title: Healthy fleet
fleet.body: Drivers are selected by highest VQI per vehicle type, connecting predictive maintenance and routing.

CAR_ONLY.note: Narrow alleys are inaccessible; requires a van

MOTORCYCLE_ONLY.note: Dense alleys and housing; motorcycles are more agile

BOTH.note: Assigned to the lighter set during allocation

methodology.routeOptimizationDescription: Nearest-neighbor round trip from the warehouse.
methodology.emissionsDescription: CO₂ by engine type × total distance
methodology.dtiDescription: End-to-end SLA: receivedAt → deliveredAt vs planned
methodology.cfiDescription: 100 = EV-equivalent; 0 = diesel over the same distance
methodology.optimizationSteps:
1. Start at warehouse ({warehouse})
2. Pick the nearest unvisited stop (by drive time)
3. Repeat until all stops are visited
4. Return to the warehouse
methodology.optimizationNote: Demo heuristic — production systems often use OR-Tools or similar tools for larger fleets. Suitable for up to 15 stops per route.
methodology.calibrationNote: OSRM calibration ×{factor}; per-stop service {minutes} min (parking + handover).
methodology.fuelDescription: Pertamina DKI Jakarta prices (live or fallback) are matched to each vehicle type. Trip costs appear across route planning and logistics dashboards, and
methodology.baselineNote: The naive baseline models a separate warehouse round trip per stop without route sharing. Optimized routes use nearest-neighbor TSP distance. The demo EV fleet uses Polytron Fox, DFSK Gelora E, and Wuling Formo Max EV.
methodology.geographyNote: Order coordinates are validated against Greater Jakarta (Jabodetabek) bounds. Demo addresses use real street coordinates.
methodology.selectionDescription: For each route chunk, the system picks the highest-VQI available driver with the matching vehicle type. See also
methodology.referencesDescription: Routing uses rule-based heuristics adapted for the Jakarta last-mile demo. Traffic calibration reflects typical urban delivery speeds, not real-time probe data unless Google Maps is connected.

referenceNotes.vrp: The classic framework for optimizing multi-stop routes from a depot.
referenceNotes.osrm: The road-distance engine used as the demo's default source.
referenceNotes.google: Optional live traffic and road polylines for map visualization.
referenceNotes.lastMile: Operational context for last-mile delivery in dense cities such as Jakarta.

methodology.dtiVariance: Variance drivers include traffic, weather, stop service time, warehouse preparation delay, route deviation, vehicle reliability, and address accuracy.
methodology.reportsDescription: Logistics KPIs aggregate DTI, CFI, fuel cost, and route metrics across active and completed routes. Charts appear on the dashboards, with exportable CSV and print layouts under
methodology.routeReportDetail: route ID, driver, vehicle, stops, distance, duration, average DTI and CFI, fuel cost, and savings against the naive baseline.
methodology.deliveryReportDetail: per-stop order ID, status, planned versus actual lead time, DTI score, and allocated emissions (CFI).
methodology.cvRoadmapDescription: ODOL Detection and Hub Congestion Detection are planned for overload monitoring and hub queue analytics. Routing metrics currently remain independent of CV inputs.
methodology.visualizeSuffix: in server environment variables to render waypoints and road-following polylines on Google Maps. See also
methodology.emissionsPreview: emissions per route on the preview card.

methodology.title: Fleet metrics & guide
methodology.subtitle: How the Vehicle Quality Index (VQI) works, why it helps manage a logistics fleet, and how scores feed routing driver dispatch (FLO v0.2).
methodology.reduceDowntimeBody: Spot high-risk vehicles before they break down, so fleets keep moving and deliveries stay on schedule.
methodology.optimizeCostBody: Prioritize spending on units that need it most instead of fixed, calendar-based servicing.
methodology.planAheadBody: Predicted next-maintenance dates turn reactive repairs into scheduled, budgeted work.
methodology.prioritizeRiskBody: A single 0-100 score ranks the whole fleet, so limited workshop capacity goes where it matters.
methodology.vqiDescription: Every vehicle starts at a perfect 100. Four factors subtract penalty points. The remaining score is the VQI.
methodology.vehicleAgeMeasures: How far through its expected life (in years) the vehicle is.
methodology.odometerWearMeasures: Distance travelled vs. expected lifetime distance, adjusted per engine type.
methodology.maintenanceCostMeasures: This vehicle's cost relative to the fleet average, adjusted per engine type.
methodology.maintenancePlanningMeasures: How many days overdue the next scheduled maintenance is.
methodology.formulaDescription: Each penalty is capped at its maximum before being subtracted.
methodology.engineModifiersDescription: Different powertrains wear and cost differently.
methodology.engineNote: EVs have fewer wear parts (lower odometer penalty); diesel units trend slightly higher on both wear and cost.
methodology.routingDispatchDescription: The same VQI score powers driver selection on Plan Route: for each route chunk, the highest-VQI available driver of the matching vehicle type (car or motorcycle) is ranked first. Dispatch shows all candidates with a selection reason. Manage drivers at
methodology.selectionRule: sort by VQI descending within vehicle type; skip drivers already assigned or inactive.
methodology.demoEv: Polytron Fox (electric motorcycle) and DFSK Gelora E / Wuling Formo Max EV (electric van) receive lower odometer/cost penalties and higher CFI scores on routes.
methodology.liveCalculationDescription: Pick a vehicle to see exactly how its VQI is derived from real data.
methodology.referencesDescription: The VQI is a rule-based scoring model adapted from established fleet replacement-scoring practice (inverted so a higher score means a healthier vehicle). It is a demo heuristic, not a copy of any single standard; machine-learning health indexing is the roadmap for a future phase.
methodology.industryModelsDescription: Fleet replacement-scoring systems that use the same factor family.
methodology.academicLiteratureDescription: Prognostics & Health Management research on health indices and RUL.
